subject: Clarifying multi-tenant chat session learning boundaries and ops evidence
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@careco.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: CareCo Legal <legal@careco.health>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: written commitment on no-model-learning for multi-tenant chat sessions

Hi Michael/David,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. To summarize CareCo's ask so we can move this through procurement/legal quickly: we need a written commitment that interactions from our multi-tenant chat product will not be used to improve or train models (no-model-learning / no-adaptive-training). Specifics we care about:

- Clear scope: exclude any training or gradient updates using our raw prompts or responses, across both text and attachments.
- Retention: session transcripts should not be retained beyond operational troubleshooting; preferred max retention 24 hours unless a customer opts in.
- Subprocessors: a short list of subprocessors that touch inference data (inference fleet, logging, SRE) and an onshore/offshore split.
- Evidence: examples of how Redwood enforces no-learning in multitenant settings (ops runbook, KV cache behavior, isolation architecture).
- SLA/credits: if this requires configuration that affects routing/throughput, we need clarity on any SLA implications and whether credits are available for the extra controls.

I attached our security questionnaire for context. Can you confirm what you can commit in writing and any evidence artifacts you can provide?

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform Security, CareCo Health
[Attachment: CareCo-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@careco.health>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: written commitment on no-model-learning for multi-tenant chat sessions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire. We can absolutely walk through a practical commitment and operational evidence. High-level response now, details and artifacts next week: 

1) Commitment scope (what we can put in DPA addendum):
   - Redwood will not use tenant session data from CareCo multi-tenant chat sessions to train or adapt any models in our hosted inference product, including fine-tuning, continuous adaptation, or model weight updates ("no-model-learning").
   - We will exclude prompts, responses, and file attachments from any training pipelines.

2) Operational controls (evidence we can provide):
   - Ephemeral KV cache: KV entries for live sessions are stored in ephemeral caches and evicted within 24 hours; we can provide screenshots and a short ops runbook excerpt.
   - Inference telemetry separation: aggregate telemetry (latency/error) is retained for product health; raw prompts/responses are not fed into training queues.
   - KMS & access controls: keys for customer data are managed via tenant-scoped KMS; we can provide a high-level key-access matrix and redactedsample audit logs.

3) Subprocessors & residency: we will provide a list of subprocessors that touch inference data and an onshore/offshore breakdown. If CareCo requires onshore-only subprocessors for inference, we can discuss Dedicated or Private deployment options.

4) SLA/credits: enabling additional isolation or onshore routing can affect capacity planning. We typically offer service credits for SLA misses; for specific commitments tied to capacity we should align with procurement on commit-levels and pricing.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll pull together a short "no-model-learning" ops evidence pack (SOC2 pointer, ops runbook excerpt, sample audit log) and share it by 2027-05-03.
- Kimberly from Legal will draft DPA addendum language.
- David (infra) will confirm the technical isolation details for multi-tenant KV behavior.

Attaching a short stub ops playbook for internal reference.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-no-learn-ops-stub.pdf (doc)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: written commitment on no-model-learning for multi-tenant chat sessions

Quick internal note on the tech side (cc'ing Kimberly so legal has context):

- Multi-tenant inference design: requests are routed to shared inference pools. We do not materialize a combined training dataset from live sessions. There are two main telemetry paths: 
  1) Aggregated metrics (latency, error) — kept for product health and aggregated at service level.
  2) Raw interaction traces — these are written to short-lived KV shards used only for cache/hot-replay and evicted per retention policy.

- No internal pipeline currently subscribes these KV shards for any model-training jobs. Training jobs run from separate data ingestion pipelines that require explicit onboarding/consent and go through the model-onboarding review.

- Evidence artifacts I can share: sample eviction logs showing TTL enforcement, a sanitized audit trail for key access to the KV store, and a diagram showing pipeline separation.

If CareCo needs stricter guarantees (e.g., no shared inference pools at all), that pushes us toward Dedicated or Private options which we should price separately.

-David

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@careco.health>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed DPA addendum language and follow-ups

Hi Elena — thanks for raising this. I’ve drafted suggested language we can use as an addendum to the standard DPA; summary below and I’ll attach a word doc with redlines in the next message if that’s helpful.

Proposed points (summary):
- "No-Model-Learning Provision": Redwood covenants that CareCo tenant interaction data will not be used to update, retrain, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any production or research model unless CareCo provides prior written consent.
- "Retention & Operational Usage": Redwood may retain session data only for operational troubleshooting and security purposes, and will purge per agreed TTL (default 24 hours). Any retention beyond that requires explicit customer consent and documented justification.
- "Subprocessor Limitation": Redwood will maintain and provide a list of subprocessors touching inference data and will notify CareCo 30 days in advance of changes. If CareCo requires onshore-only subprocessors for inference and logging, Redwood will propose a Dedicated/Private offering.
- "Evidence and Audit Rights": Redwood will provide an annual evidence pack (SOC2 pointer + runbook excerpts) and on-request redacted audit logs to validate eviction/access.

Questions for CareCo: is an annual evidence pack + on-request redacted logs sufficient, or do you require periodic live attestations? Also, can we align on SLA targets so we understand when capacity/credits need to be negotiated?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena.park@careco.health>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: CareCo Legal <legal@careco.health>, procurement@careco.health
Date: 2027-05-04T08:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA addendum language and follow-ups

Kimberly/Michael — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- The No-Model-Learning Provision and 24-hour default TTL look acceptable as long as you can provide the eviction logs and a redacted audit trail on request.
- Annual evidence pack + on-request redacted logs is fine for legal, but our security team will want a one-time live walkthrough of the ops runbook prior to execution.
- SLA: we need a 99.9% inference availability target for the production route used by our customers; if enabling onshore subprocessors or extra isolation causes degradation we will expect proportional credits. Please have procurement confirm typical credit levels or options.

If you can send the DPA addendum redline and the ops evidence pack this week, we can take it to insiders/legal for sign-off. Attaching our DPA addendum request doc for reference.

Thanks,
Elena
[Attachment: CareCo-DPA-addendum-request.docx (doc)]
